supersededTokens.reason: First SKOOP PunchCard deploy used correct bytecode behavior but stale/misleading verified-source comments inherited from the factory path.
supersededTokens._disposal_note: NOT burned. The disposal tx is transfer(0x000...dEaD, 100000000e6), selector 0xa9059cbb — verified on-chain 2026-09-19. totalSupply() on the superseded token still reads 100,000,000.000000 and always will, so Basescan shows it as a live token with one holder. The supply is unrecoverable because nobody holds the dead address's key, but it was never destroyed. MerchantToken is ERC20Burnable and burn() would have set supply to zero; it is no longer callable because the owner wallet no longer holds the tokens.

wallets._owner_note: Holds the entire supply. Becomes ownerWallet on the escrow, treasury and locker - immutable in all three - and is the only address that can ever call evacuateLP(). Highest-stakes key in the system.

Call lockLP() yet. SKOOP keeps LP recoverability with no deadline while the network is in beta - decided 2026-09-16. Closing it is the intent once the system has proven itself, not a decision against ever closing it. lockLP() is one-way; after it the pilot locker behaves identically to production. evacuationOpen() is the on-chain source of truth and every surface must read it rather than assert a state.
